patch.value: pm activity answers what happened to one item in the last half hour when the agent asked what changed in the workspace: 20 rows cover 5 of the 272 items touched in 24 hours and none carries a title

Measured on the live tracker: the default bound is 20 rows over an unfiltered reverse-chronological merge of all 2443 history streams. Those 20 rows resolve to 5 distinct items spanning 27 minutes, while 757 events across 272 distinct items landed in the preceding 24 hours - so the default names 1.8 percent of the items touched in a day. Rows carry id, op, ts and author only, so rebuilding context costs one pm get per id, and 18 of the 20 carry no message at all. The op vocabulary is dominated by mechanical sub-mutations: update 25.1 percent, comment_add 18.8, files_add 15.4, tests_add 7.1, claim 6.4, release 5.4 - more than half the window is attachment and lock churn rather than lifecycle change, and the lock verb release reads as a version release. An item-centric digest over a time window (one row per item touched, carrying type, status, event count, last timestamp, a bounded op summary and the title) covers 15 items in 2426 bytes against the current 2918 bytes for 5. The join is already paid for: prepareActivityHistoryRead already reads every item light metadata record to enforce the history-stream policy and then discards everything except the ids.

Default pm activity returns one row per item touched inside a declared time window, carrying id, type, status, event count, first and last timestamp, a bounded op summary and the title, ordered by recency or event count; The envelope declares the window plus event, item and author totals and a bounded op histogram, so an agent can distinguish a quiet period from a truncated one; The raw per-event stream stays reachable behind an explicit flag with the compact row shape unchanged, and --full, --provenance and the existing filters are unaffected; Item metadata is joined from the light metadata read the command already performs, adding no second traversal, and the digest cost is asserted by the token-budget-gate corpus; Contracts snapshot, completion scripts, MCP surface and docs are regenerated in the same change

message: Filed from a measured read of pm activity default output and the full history corpus on the live tracker

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Measurement and implementation map, taken on the live tracker at 2026-08-11 over all 47448 history entries in 2443 streams.

What the default actually returns
- 20 rows, resolving to 5 distinct items and 8 op kinds, spanning 27 minutes.
- 2 of those 20 rows carry a message; the other 18 carry id, op, ts and author only.
- Widening the row bound does not help: the last 50 entries still resolve to 5 items, the last 100 to 5, the last 200 to 8. The stream is bursty per item, so a row-denominated bound is the wrong unit for a workspace question.

What the same period actually contains
- last 24 hours: 757 events, 272 distinct items, 2 authors.
- last 72 hours: 1841 events, 327 items.
- last 7 days: 3354 events, 432 items.
- Daily volume over the last week runs 223 to 746 events.

Op distribution over the whole corpus
update 25.1 percent, comment_add 18.8, files_add 15.4, tests_add 7.1, claim 6.4, release 5.4, close 5.2, create 5.1, docs_add 3.5, test_run_track 2.4, note_add 1.7, learning_add 1.5, then a long tail. More than half of every window is attachment and lock churn. The two ops that carry lifecycle meaning, create and close, are 10.3 percent combined. The lock verb release is also the word for a version release, which is a second reason the raw op column misleads on sight.

Proposed default, measured
One row per item touched in a declared window, carrying id, type, status, event count, last timestamp, a bounded op summary and a truncated title, plus a header declaring the window, event, item and author totals and a top-N op histogram. Rendered at 15 rows this is 2426 bytes against the current 2918 bytes, so it names three times as many items for 17 percent fewer bytes, and each row is actionable without a follow-up pm get.

Implementation map
- The item join is already paid for. prepareActivityHistoryRead in the activity module already calls the light item-metadata reader to enforce the history-stream policy, then keeps only the ids and discards the titles, types and statuses the digest needs. No second traversal is required.
- The folding is a group-by over entries already collected by collectActivityEntries, before the row bound is applied. Today the bound is applied to entries; the digest applies it to items.
- The default bound constants live beside the command as separate compact and full values, so a third digest default fits the existing shape.
- The projection block already declares mode and row_key for compact, provenance and full, so a fourth mode is an extension of a declared contract rather than a new concept.
- The read-output projection table already lists the three activity row keys, and a digest row key has to be added there or the published selector will not find the rows.
- The token-budget-gate corpus already carries an activity-default entry, so the digest cost is measurable against an existing baseline instead of a new one.

Scope boundary
This is not the delta-read feature. pm-tuadp2 owns --since cursor deltas for list, search, context and get. This item owns only what pm activity returns by default. pm-tqel owns the eventual consolidation of the history verbs under one noun and is unaffected by the row shape chosen here.
